subject: ClearFleet — inference cost pressure, pilot proposal & telemetry asks
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@clearfleet.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 14:15:00 -0500
Subject: ClearFleet kickoff — inference cost pressure, pilot proposal & telemetry asks

Hi Mark —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we’re aligned and so the Eng/Proc teams at ClearFleet have what they need to move quickly. I captured the pain points, goals, and proposed next steps below.

Pain points you shared
- Token-driven spend is ballooning (3–4x YoY); current OpenAI spend is the single biggest infra line item for ML infra.
- Latency spikes at peak (bursty traffic) lead to timeouts and client retries — amplifies cost.
- No systematic prefix/KV caching in front of inference; some ad-hoc app-side caching but inconsistent.

Current stack (what you described)
- Frontend -> caching layer (Redis + CDN) -> transform layer -> OpenAI API (mostly GPT-4 family)
- Batch jobs for nightly re-ranks; live requests mostly single-shot generations
- Telemetry: sampling traces pushed to Datadog; token counts and raw latencies available in logs

Success criteria (how ClearFleet will measure pilot success)
- Reduce per-token unit cost by ~35–45% for the most common gen workload without regressing quality beyond 1–2% NLI/hand-eval hit rate.
- Keep p95 latency <= 350ms for production traffic during pilot window.
- Operational: Redwood integrates with existing telemetry and can demonstrate stable handling at your 3k RPS burst profile.

Technical openness / constraints
- You’re open to quantized model variants if quality holds (willing to evaluate INT8 and experimental INT4 but would need guardrails).
- Cache-first approach preferred; you want Redwood to be able to consider both edge prefix caching and on-host KV caches.
- Data residency: logs/telemetry remain in your account; any sample data exported to Redwood will be scrubbed.

Proposed next steps (high level)
1) NDA + telemetry access: you mentioned sending a signed NDA then sharing a small sample of Datadog traces + token histograms.
2) Pilot SOW (2 weeks): Redwood runs a 2-week pilot to measure unit economics across three model variants (baseline full precision, INT8 quant, experimental INT4) with automatic batching and KV cache enabled. I attached a pilot SOW template and a simple cost model spreadsheet.
3) Pilot kickoff: target start Jan 26 — we’ll run smoke tests week 0 and full traffic week 1.
4) Success review: short readout and cost/quality matrix at end of pilot; if metrics meet thresholds, we’ll provide a pricing proposal and options for Dedicated capacity.

Immediate asks from us to you
- Please confirm the Eng lead who’ll be the primary contact for telemetry and access (we’ll need a short-lived API key and a link to a sample Datadog dashboard).
- If procurement needs a high-level SOW ahead of internal approvals, we can provide one for signatures — attached.

Attachments: pilot-sow-template.docx, ClearFleet_MAI_Metrics.xlsx (simple cost model)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options for Jan 26 for the kickoff readiness call.

Best,
Avery Johnson

On Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 4:03 PM Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@clearfleet.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Avery — this is a great summary.
> 
> Quick notes: 1) can you explain briefly how Redwood handles prefix caching when most of our cache is CDN + Redis (we prefer to keep caching within our VPC), and 2) is INT4 something you’ve run in production or is it experimental-only right now?

Hi Mark & Lena —

Short answers:
- Prefix/KV caching: Redwood supports hybrid caching. For a setup like yours we typically recommend (and can support) a VPC-resident KV cache (Redis or native KV) with an optional small edge cache to reduce RTT. The cache is pluggable — we won’t require moving your primary cache. During the pilot we can enable cache warmers and a sampling proxy so your team retains control of cache keys and TTLs.

- Quantization (INT8/INT4): INT8 quantization is supported broadly across our verified model profiles and is production-ready on several model families with negligible quality impact in our evals. INT4 is experimental: we’ve run customer pilots (low-volume) with INT4 where quality/regression profiles vary by prompt; we recommend guardrails: A/B holdout slices + automatic fallback to INT8 or fp16 on quality regression. We will surface per-prompt deltas in the pilot readout.

Pilot configuration proposal (concrete)
- Window: 2 weeks (smoke tests day 0, full run days 1–14)
- Traffic: emulate your peak burst profile (target 3k RPM peak, average ~800 RPS during business hours)
- Models: baseline fp16 (your current), INT8 quant, experimental INT4 (QA gating)
- Metrics: per-token cost, p50/p95 latency, end-to-end success (hand-eval + simple automatic quality checks), cache hit-rate impact

Action items for next steps
- Mark/Lena: please share sample Datadog traces + token histogram and the telemetry contact (we only need read-only access / short-lived token).
- Legal/procurement: we’ll resend an NDA and the SOW template; procurement can use the attached SOW (pilot-sow-template.docx) and we’re happy to follow your internal sign-off flow.

I’m copying Rishi from our infra team — he’ll run technical onboarding and smoke tests.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
